question: Should OpenClaw accept this bundled 1Password SecretRef resolver, including its service-account-token-to-local-`op` executable boundary and new `@openclaw/fs-safe` dependency, for the reviewed head?
rationale: The implementation is technically bounded and proof-positive, but accepting a bundled privileged executable path and dependency graph is a repository security and product ownership choice rather than a mechanical contributor repair.

options.title: Authorize the bounded integration
options.body: Approve the exact reviewed head after security confirms the executable-trust model and dependency graph are acceptable for a bundled opt-in plugin.

options.title: Keep the broker-only scope
options.body: Decline the SecretRef provider surface and retain the existing curated agent broker without adding local `op` execution for config credentials.

recommendation.title: Authorize the bounded integration
recommendation.body: Approve the exact reviewed head after security confirms the executable-trust model and dependency graph are acceptable for a bundled opt-in plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository's dependency guard explicitly identifies this group as an authorization path for the changed dependency graph and associated security review.
